description: Quick picks next to the five official fields (T65): stars that visibly move within SPHEREx's coverage, and nearby brown dwarfs whose spectrum is the interesting part. Built by web/make_discover.py; the official fields are in presets.json.
method: SIMBAD J2000 ICRS + proper motion propagated linearly to epoch 2026.0, rounded to 1e-4 deg; one per system (10'); shift_px = proper motion x (last - first SPHEREx exposure there) / 6.15"; moving stars need shift_px >= 0.75, brown dwarfs K (Vega) <= 13.5, sorted by K

provenance.query: SELECT TOP 150 b.main_id, b.ra, b.dec, b.pmra, b.pmdec, b.otype, b.plx_value, (b.pmra*b.pmra + b.pmdec*b.pmdec) AS pm2, fk.flux AS k FROM basic AS b LEFT OUTER JOIN flux AS fk ON fk.oidref = b.oid AND fk.filter = 'K' WHERE b.pmra*b.pmra + b.pmdec*b.pmdec > 9000000 AND b.otype NOT IN ('Pl', 'Pl?', 'err') ORDER BY pm2 DESC

SELECT TOP 150 b.main_id, b.ra, b.dec, b.pmra, b.pmdec, b.otype, b.plx_value, (b.pmra*b.pmra + b.pmdec*b.pmdec) AS pm2, fk.flux AS k FROM basic AS b LEFT OUTER JOIN flux AS fk ON fk.oidref = b.oid AND fk.filter = 'K' WHERE b.otype IN ('BD*', 'BD?') AND b.pmra*b.pmra + b.pmdec*b.pmdec > 1000000 ORDER BY pm2 DESC

SELECT j.id AS main, i.id AS name FROM ident AS i JOIN ident AS j ON i.oidref = j.oidref WHERE j.id IN ('HD  33793', 'HD 103095', 'HD 217987', 'HD 225213', '*  61 Cyg A', 'NAME Teegarden''s Star', 'HD  95735', '2MASS J16465480-1358175', 'Wolf  359', 'V* AX Mic', 'NAME L 362-29 BC', '2MASS J15551573-0956055', '2MASS J14392836+1929149', 'DENIS J025503.3-470049', '2MASSI J1300425+191235', '2MASS J02511490-0352459', '2MASSW J1506544+132106', 'SSSPM J1444-2019', 'DENIS J125310.8-570924', '2MASS J10224821+5825453') AND i.id LIKE 'NAME %'

fields.name: Kapteyn's star
fields.group: Fastest-moving stars
fields.why: High proper-motion star, 13 light-years away. Moves 8.6″ a year: about 1.5 SPHEREx pixels between the first and last epoch here (2025-08-10 → 2026-09-07, 3 epochs). Small: blink the first against the last epoch, the name and its path show where it goes. It is bright, so its saturated core shows as a gap that moves with it.

fields.name: L 362-29 BC
fields.group: Brown dwarfs: look at the spectrum
fields.why: Brown dwarf, 40 light-years away. Moves 1.6″ a year, only 0.3 px in SPHEREx's coverage here (2025-05-21 → 2026-06-07, 3 epochs): too little to see in a blink (the name shows its path). Look at its spectrum instead: a brown dwarf doesn't follow a star's shape (water and methane absorb) and is bright at 4–5 µm.
